| [THEORY-045](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-045.md) | Felt affect is the experience of the body's regulatory state, valenced by what that state means for staying alive and present throughout waking experience, not only in emotion; whether what is felt is a prediction of that state or a map of it is unsettled | Barrett (2017), [LIT-542](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-542.md), and Damasio & Carvalho (2013), [LIT-388](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-388.md), are two independent accounts that agree on a base layer. What is felt as affect (valence and arousal for Barrett, feeling for Damasio) is the body's regulatory state. Its valence is that state's value for the organism, and it is present in hunger, pain and well-being as much as in emotion. They disagree about what the experience is of. For Barrett it is the brain's allostatic prediction of the body, issued from agranular limbic cortex. For Damasio it is a topographic map of the body's state, built in the upper brainstem, and their paper makes no use of prediction. Seth ([LIT-135](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-135.md)) builds on the same base but makes his claim about consciousness, not about affect. Friston ([LIT-526](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-526.md)) supports neither. Proposed: both sources are theoretical syntheses, and neither tests the claim. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-059](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-059.md) | The readiness potential does not show that a neural decision to act precedes awareness of the urge to act | Libet read the readiness potential, which begins half a second or more before a spontaneous movement and before the reported urge, as the brain deciding first. Two independent arguments in the record remove that inference. Schurger, Sitt & Dehaene ([LIT-605](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-605.md)) show that a leaky accumulator driven by noise and fitted to waiting times alone reproduces the averaged readiness potential (r² = 0.96), because movement-locked averaging recovers the fluctuations that crossed threshold; a prediction of theirs held in 13 people. Dennett & Kinsbourne ([LIT-431](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-431.md)) argue that the clock report times a represented content, not an event in the brain. Proposed: the authors say their model shows the potential could be fluctuation, not that it is. It says nothing about whether the urge causes the act. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-062](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-062.md) | Model-based and model-free predictions both operate in instrumental and in Pavlovian learning, and which one controls behaviour follows their relative reliability, not the preference of a supervising system | Daw, Niv & Dayan ([LIT-580](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-580.md)) cast habitual and goal-directed instrumental control as model-free caching and model-based search, and let behaviour follow whichever estimate is less uncertain; simulations reproduce the effects of over-training, task complexity and reward proximity on devaluation. Dayan & Berridge ([LIT-584](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-584.md)) show from instant revaluation of a salt cue that Pavlovian prediction also has a model-based form, and suggest the same reliability arbitration there. Both controllers pursue the same ends; neither is the irrational one. The instrumental half is qualitative simulation; the Pavlovian half of the arbitration is a suggestion. Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-063](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-063.md) | The unity of experience is the integration of one global world-model into a single functional cluster, and it does not require a self-model | Metzinger's précis of Being No One (2005), [LIT-568](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-568.md): the globality constraint makes every conscious content part of one world-model. On the functional level that is "highest-order binding" into a single causal role, and on the neural level the prediction of "one single area of maximal causal density", after Tononi and Edelman's dynamic core. "What you subjectively experience upon experiencing your world as coherent is the high internal correlation strength between a subset of physical events in your own brain." A unified world comes before a self: the minimal case is "Selfless Snapshot Consciousness", and fully depersonalized states are "non-subjective consciousness". The neural half is a cited hypothesis, the précis says little is known, and how the cluster becomes one subject's is left open. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-070](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-070.md) | How much cognitive control to exert, and on what, is decided by a cost-benefit computation (the expected value of control) in a specification system distinct from the structures that implement the control | Shenhav, Botvinick & Cohen ([LIT-585](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-585.md)) unify dACC's many reported functions as one: deciding whether, where and how much control to allocate. A control signal has an identity (a task set, a threshold, an attention template) and an intensity; its expected value is its probability-weighted payoff, with future value discounted, minus an intrinsic cost rising with intensity. dACC monitors and specifies; lateral prefrontal and subcortical structures implement. The paper reviews evidence and fits nothing, so Proposed. It does not say what the cost is, how EVC is computed, or that it governs emotion regulation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-088](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-088.md) | Slow large-scale activity in human cortex is organised as in a pattern-forming medium: its flow is set by interacting spiral defects centred on phase singularities, which sit on boundaries between functional regions, annihilate with spirals of opposite rotation and repel those of the same | Xu, Long, Feng & Gong (2023), [LIT-638](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-638.md): in Human Connectome Project fMRI band-passed to 0.01–0.1 Hz, the cortical phase field holds about 16–19 spirals at a time around phase singularities, concentrated on boundaries between functional regions; their centres drift superdiffusively, opposite spirals annihilate (51% fully, 46% partly) and like ones repel (2.6%), and their positions and senses decode task condition above a raw-amplitude decoder. One source, fMRI only, at a spatial scale chosen because it maximised that decoding; the routing of activity flow is read from phase gradients and a phase-oscillator model, never perturbed. The kinship with Belousov–Zhabotinsky spirals and pattern-formation defects is the record's analogy, not the paper's. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-090](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-090.md) | A basic, affective form of consciousness is realised subcortically, in the upper brainstem and thalamus, before and without cortex, and its first function is alarm: survival behaviour, care for the body and generalised one-shot learning, with no choice between options | Newen & Montemayor's ALARM theory (2025), [LIT-626](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-626.md): basic arousal, a sensitivity to pain, pleasure and other basic affect without focused attention, can be realised without cortex, by the upper brainstem and thalamus, and its function is to alarm the bodily agent when a homeostatic variable leaves its range, giving the signal "100% weight" through "rather rigid behavioural programmes without choices". Damasio & Carvalho (2013), [LIT-388](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-388.md), supply the subcortical clause independently: feeling is generated in the upper brainstem and the insula is not needed. Both papers argue from cited evidence and offer no new data, and neither has a marker that tells a felt alarm from an unfelt one. The function clause rests on ALARM alone, and Veit's account rivals it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-093](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-093.md) | A content of mind is conscious when a continuous flow of homeostatic feelings identifies it as the organism's own; the feelings are conscious in themselves and hybrid, partly made of the body state they map, because interoceptive pathways let the body act directly on the neurons that map it | Damasio & Damasio (2022), [LIT-628](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-628.md), an essay with no data, read only through a summarising fetch tool, so its wording is paraphrased here. Consciousness is the spontaneous identification of mind contents as belonging to one's own organism, and a continuous stream of homeostatic feelings, from hunger and pain to a faint feeling of existing, supplies it; the feelings are conscious in themselves and confer consciousness on exteroceptive images. They are hybrid because interoceptive axons are unmyelinated, partly non-synaptic and outside a systematic blood–brain barrier, so viscera and circulating molecules act on the neurons that map them. Damasio & Carvalho (2013), [LIT-388](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-388.md), read in full, supply the upper-brainstem site of feeling and the unmyelinated-fibre proposal. Proposed: the identification is a definition, the mechanism an interpretation of anatomy, and the clinical evidence does not separate this account from its rivals. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-094](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-094.md) | Neither report nor no-report paradigms isolate the neural basis of consciousness, because post-perceptual cognition that tracks the percept persists without report; only a design that removes differential post-perceptual cognition does | Block (2007), [LIT-646](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-646.md), framed the methodological puzzle: the neural basis of experience can be found only by deciding whether it includes the machinery of access, and the evidence comes through report. The no-report paradigm was the answer. Block (2019), [LIT-637](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-637.md), argues it has "a fatal flaw": subjects not asked to report still think about what they see, and that thought is aligned with the percept (the "bored monkey" problem). Eliminating report isolates the basis of experience "only if it eliminates post-perceptual cognitive processing" correlated with the percept. Brascamp et al.'s inconspicuous rivalry, whose switches subjects detected at chance, is the one such design Block offers. The method is specific to rivalry so far, and Block says there may be no general solution. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-096](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-096.md) | Perceptual consciousness is global availability: a content becomes conscious when the activity it drives into a core of long-range hub neurons, prefrontal among them, crosses a threshold and ignites it, so that the network amplifies, sustains and broadcasts that one content to the specialised processors; below threshold it leaves a decaying wave and is not experienced | Mashour, Roelfsema, Changeux & Dehaene (2020), [LIT-631](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-631.md), a review by the theory's proponents. Conscious access is "a non-linear network ignition" that amplifies and sustains a representation so that local processors can access it, in a distributed core of long-range layer II/III and V pyramidal neurons with prefrontal cortex a key hub but "not ... the exclusive territory". Ignition is exclusive: one content at a time. Evidence: seen and unseen trials diverge after about 200 ms across modalities; in van Vugt et al.'s monkeys, missed stimuli drove V1 and V4 but only reported ones, and false alarms, ignited sustained prefrontal firing, and the signal-detection threshold is the ignition threshold. The review adopts the premise that global availability "is what we subjectively experience as a conscious state", and calls experience without access untested; that premise, not the access data, is where it rivals overflow and the sensory account. Single source, second-hand evidence, and the P3 question conceded open. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-097](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-097.md) | Long-range coordination in the human forebrain is carried by brief ripples that co-occur at distant sites: during them neurons co-fire more whatever the distance between them, and at retrieval they carry stimulus-specific reinstatement of encoding co-firing | Verzhbinsky, Daume, Cheng, Rutishauser & Halgren (2026), [LIT-633](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-633.md): in 1,373 single units from five bilateral forebrain regions of 35 epilepsy patients doing a Sternberg task, ripples (70–100 Hz, about 70 ms) co-occur between bundles at a median 5% at every tract distance from 71 to 223 mm, and unit pairs co-fire a median 34% more during co-ripples than in no-ripple periods, beyond a rate-only null and with no loss over distance. The gain rises with load (13% in maintenance, 19% at retrieval), and encoding co-firing for a stimulus recurs at retrieval in 0.29% of cell-pair trials in co-ripples against 0.14% outside them. Correlational throughout: one task, two load levels, clinically placed electrodes, nothing perturbed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-098](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-098.md) v3 | The neural basis of perceptual consciousness does not include the prefrontal machinery of cognitive access: it is recurrent activity in sensory cortex | Block's "back of the head" position, from three papers. Block (2005), [LIT-629](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-629.md): a phenomenal NCC (for seen motion, recurrent MT/V5–V1 activity) and an access NCC (frontoparietal broadcasting), with winner-take-all access letting a recurrent sensory representation lose and stay unaccessed. Block (2007), [LIT-646](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-646.md): the mesh argument. If workspace activation is not part of the basis of experience, strong losing sensory coalitions explain why experience overflows access; if it is, nothing does. Block (2019), [LIT-637](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-637.md): no-report designs do not settle the prefrontal question, because thought about the percept persists, and one design that removes it found no prefrontal difference by fMRI, which Block calls evidence against prefrontalism while granting that ECoG could still support it. Proposed: an inference to the best explanation, with every experiment second-hand and the decisive test not yet run. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-100](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-100.md) | A neural correlate of conscious report does not require laminar cortex: in crows it is carried by the nidopallium caudolaterale, a nuclear pallial region whose neurons follow the reported percept rather than the stimulus | Maldarelli & Güntürkün (2025), [LIT-650](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-650.md), reviewing Nieder et al. (2020): in crows reporting near-threshold stimuli, single neurons in the nidopallium caudolaterale (NCL), the functional analogue of prefrontal cortex, fired with the "seen" report whether or not a stimulus was shown and were silent on "not seen" reports. NCL is nuclear, not layered; the cortex-like layers and columns found in birds are confined to the sensory pallium. So a correlate of conscious report does not need laminar cortex. The crow evidence is second-hand, from one laboratory and not in the record, and a report paradigm cannot separate access from phenomenal consciousness. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-102](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-102.md) | In human ventral temporal cortex the category and object identity of a clearly seen, unchanging image are carried for as long as it stays on by a stable population code while activity amplitude decays; prefrontal and parietal content is a transient event at onset | Vishne, Gerber, Knight & Deouell (2023), [LIT-644](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-644.md): in 430 visually responsive subdural electrodes from 10 patients viewing images for 300–1,500 ms with no report on analysed trials, high-frequency activity and single-electrode category selectivity fell about 80% from peak by 800–900 ms, while the pattern across ventral temporal electrodes kept near-ceiling, time-invariant category and exemplar information that ended a fixed delay after the image went off. Prefrontal and parietal information was confined to about 150–600 ms and ignored duration. This met the predictions both IIT's and the global workspace's proponents registered for the paradigm, so it did not discriminate them. Above- threshold images only, sparse right-lateralised frontal coverage, one frequency band; it does not show the code tracks experience rather than input. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-103](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-103.md) | Perceptual consciousness overflows cognitive access: in partial-report tasks more items are experienced than the roughly four that working memory holds, though any one of them can be accessed when cued | Block (2007), [LIT-646](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-646.md), and Block (2011), [LIT-640](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-640.md). Subjects shown 8–32 items say they see all or almost all of them, report about 4, and when cued after offset can report or compare most of any cued subset: capacity 6–7 of 8 up to 1.5 s (Landman et al.), and 7, 6 and 5 of 8 at 1, 2.5 and 4 s (fragile visual short-term memory), against a working memory that stays at about 4. Block reads the surplus as experienced. The rival "sparse" reading holds it in an unconscious store plus a conscious generic or fragmentary image, and Block argues there is no independent evidence for either posit. Proposed: every experiment is second-hand, and that the surplus is conscious is the contested step. Overflow means most items are unaccessed, not that any is inaccessible. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-124](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-124.md) | During a visual decision task, neurons within a single area of mouse cortex rarely form discrete functional types, yet the task conditions the area distinguishes are linearly separable in nearly every way | Posani et al. (2026), [LIT-708](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-708.md): in about 14,000 cortical units of the IBL Brainwide Map, the 8-variable selectivity profiles of 4,617 selective neurons beat a covariance-matched Gaussian null for clustering within a region only in VISp, AUDp and SSp-ul. Elsewhere the profiles form an elongated, unclustered cloud. After merging conditions a region cannot tell apart (leaving 5 to 16 of 16), ≥ 95% of random balanced dichotomies are decodable above a shuffle null in 15 of 16 regions, GU being 0.82. Types do appear when regions are pooled, aligned with anatomy. One task, overtrained mice, a lenient separability criterion. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-191](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-191.md) | In natural odour sources, the rank order of correlations between compound concentrations has the Betti-curve signature of points near the boundary of a three-dimensional hyperbolic ball, not of a uniform Euclidean cube, and human odour-descriptor profiles have that of a full three-dimensional hyperbolic ball | Zhou, Smith & Sharpee (2018), [LIT-872](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-872.md): for strawberry, tomato, blueberry and mouse-urine volatiles, and for Dravnieks' perceptual ratings of 127 odorants, clique-topology Betti curves match a 3D hyperbolic model and reject uniform Euclidean cubes of every dimension tried. It does not show a tree in the data, and because the fitted odour model is a thin shell, it does not separate a hyperbolic metric from a sphere in flat space. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-192](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-192.md) | Pairwise correlations among rat CA1 place cells have the Betti-curve signature of points sampled uniformly from a three-dimensional hyperbolic ball, not of a low-dimensional Euclidean cube, and the fitted radius grows with the logarithm of exploration time | Zhang, Rich, Lee & Sharpee (2022), [LIT-876](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-876.md): in twelve sessions from three data sets, the rank order of CA1 spike correlations matched uniform samples from a 3D hyperbolic ball and not uniform samples from low-dimensional Euclidean cubes or shuffled data, and the ball's radius rose with log exploration time from seconds to days. It does not show that the metric, as opposed to the distribution of field scales, is hyperbolic, nor that a tree is represented. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-240](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-240.md) | Loss of consciousness under propofol and in chronic disorders of consciousness goes with reduced pairwise integrated information between default-mode regions that rank as gateways of a synergy-defined workspace, not between its broadcasters | Luppi et al. (2024), [LIT-949](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-949.md), read in [NOTE-799](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-799.md). In resting-state fMRI, the regions where synergistic interactions outrank redundant ones split by rank into gateways (mainly default mode) and broadcasters (mainly fronto-parietal). Pairwise ΦR, the whole-minus-sum Φ plus redundancy, falls between default-mode gateways in propofol anaesthesia, in 22 DOC patients, and against post-anaesthetic recovery. The original Φ shows no common decrease. The finding is correlational, pairwise and content-free. The gateway/broadcaster split is imposed by the method; only where its two classes fall is measured. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-245](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-245.md) | In a preregistered multimodal test with clearly seen images, prefrontal cortex carried a seen image's category but not its identity, and its orientation at most weakly, while posterior cortex carried all three; no prefrontal site responded at stimulus offset | Cogitate Consortium, Ferrante et al. (2025), [LIT-973](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-973.md), read in [NOTE-812](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-812.md). In iEEG and fMRI, with Bayesian support for the nulls, and against a positive control, prefrontal cortex held category but no identity or orientation, and none of 655 prefrontal electrodes showed the onset-and-offset response GNWT predicted. It does not show these dimensions were unaccessed, or that prefrontal cortex lacks them in other signals: high gamma and BOLD only, no single units, and every image was seen. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-252](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-252.md) | On computational functionalism, an intervention that changes no neural activity and no actual causal interaction can change consciousness, because a clamp that stays idle on the actual input removes the transitions on every other input | Gidon, Aru and Larkum (2025), [LIT-1000](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1000.md), read in full in [NOTE-818](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-818.md): a voltage clamp replaying a recorded response injects no current on the matching stimulus yet fixes the network's transitions on every other, so on the Turing–Putnam definition the computation degenerates while nothing that happens changes. It is a conditional about the view, not evidence about experience; the simulation shows only what an ideal clamp does, and the premise that removing unexercised branches changes experience is cited, not defended. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-261](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-261.md) | In sparse distributed memory, recall of uniform random data is a signal-to-noise problem whose optimum activates about (2MT)^-1/3 of the hard locations, and capacity then grows with the number of hard locations, to about a tenth of them at 0.999 bit fidelity, not with the word length | Kanerva (1992), [LIT-921](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-921.md), §§3.5–3.7, read in full in [NOTE-779](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-779.md), after Jaeckel (1989a). An approximate derivation for uniform random data and exact retrieval cues. It does not cover noisy cues, which lower capacity, or clustered data, which the uniform design handles badly, and it does not contain the critical-distance analysis that is sometimes attributed to it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-262](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-262.md) | Neural complexity is low when a system's parts are independent or uniformly dependent and high when small subsets are nearly independent while large ones are integrated; in simulated cortex, patchy grouped connectivity raises it above random connectivity of equal density | Tononi, Sporns & Edelman (1994), [LIT-998](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-998.md), read in [NOTE-767](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-767.md). C_N, the summed shortfall of average subset integration below a linear rise with subset size, is shown low at both extremes for one family of Gaussian matrices, and higher for patchy than for uniform wiring in one simulated visual area and in small linear systems. All of it is simulation. It is a whole-system number over fixed components: it does not find units or boundaries. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-272](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-272.md) | A network of threshold units with symmetric Hebbian couplings is a content-addressable memory whose stored patterns are attractors, with limits: recall degrades near 0.15N random patterns, memories closer than about a tenth of N fuse, and overload loses every memory unless old ones are forgotten | Hopfield (1982), [LIT-918](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-918.md), read in full in [NOTE-819](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-819.md). The energy descent is derived for symmetric couplings; everything quantitative, including the 0.15N figure, the basin width and the merging distance, is simulation at N = 30 and 100. It does not say that spurious states come only from overload: they appear at a low load too. Nor does it say anything about addressed memory. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-285](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-285.md) | In an active-inference model of post-traumatic context inference, an overly precise prior that one is in a harmful context makes exploratory sampling look uninformative, so the agent attenuates the periphery, never receives the evidence that would correct the prior, and the belief sustains itself; lowering precision removes the symptoms without correcting the prior | Linson, Anderson, Markham, Friston & Moutoussis (2025), [LIT-983](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-983.md), read in version 2 in [NOTE-766](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-766.md). A mechanism shown in illustrative simulation: policy selection by expected information gain, plus a confident prior, withholds the only disambiguating observations, so the prior keeps itself up. Exposure that restores sampling rebalances it; a precision-lowering drug only suppresses symptoms. No data are fitted, parameters are unreported, and the two intervention arms differ in environment as well as mechanism. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-291](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-291.md) | The brain's visceromotor and interoceptive regions form one intrinsic system that reproduces their tract-traced anatomy and contains the hubs of the default-mode and salience networks | Theriault et al. (2025), [LIT-996](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-996.md), read in full in [NOTE-761](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-761.md), reporting the group's own 3 T (N = 550) and 7 T (N = 90) studies; Barrett (2017), [LIT-542](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-542.md), read in [NOTE-434](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-434.md), for the 3 T system. The anatomy and overlap are reported second-hand. The reading the paper adds, that the named networks' psychological labels are "destined to fail" and that the brain's primary function is allostasis, is not part of this account; the authors themselves do not claim allostasis-first is correct. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-296](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-296.md) | In a preregistered multimodal test with clearly seen images, category-selective posterior cortex showed no sustained content-specific synchronization with early visual cortex: the coupling was brief, low-frequency and mostly stimulus-evoked | Cogitate Consortium, Ferrante et al. (2025), [LIT-973](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-973.md), read in [NOTE-812](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-812.md). IIT's proponents predicted sustained gamma-band synchronization between category-selective cortex and V1/V2 throughout a conscious percept. iEEG and MEG phase consistency found only early, brief, 2–25 Hz coupling, mostly evoked, with Bayesian support for the null; exploratory amplitude coupling was also brief. V1/V2 was sparsely sampled in iEEG. It tests IIT's proposed implementation, not integrated information. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-298](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-298.md) | Report-based evidence cannot test whether posterior cortex suffices for experience, because report itself needs anterior activity, and no marker that bypasses report has a validation resting neither on introspection nor on a contested theory | Seth & Bayne (2022), [LIT-982](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-982.md), "Evaluating theories of consciousness" and Box 3, read in [NOTE-849](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-849.md) from the accepted manuscript. An argument in a review, not a result: the verification of posterior-sufficiency predictions "relies on subjective report …, which in turn requires anterior cortical activity", and validating a non-report marker by theory borrows a contested theory, by introspection, unreliable report. It says the methods are lacking "at present", not that the question is unanswerable. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-300](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-300.md) | Acting on a coercive instruction reduces the implicit sense of agency over the outcome, compared with freely choosing the same action | Haggard (2017), [LIT-1009](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1009.md), manuscript pp. 16–17 and Fig. 5, read in full in [NOTE-827](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-827.md), reporting one experiment by his group (Caspar et al. 2016). Under an experimenter's instruction to press the key that shocked a co-participant, the perceived action–tone interval was longer and the auditory N1 to the tone smaller than under free choice. It shows a reduced experience of agency, not reduced responsibility, and the review says so. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-302](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-302.md) | Coordinated action is controlled by tuning relatively autonomous coordinative structures, not by commanding muscles: a higher level specifies an equivalence class of acceptable states and sets the parameters of self-regulating units, leaving the realized details to them | Turvey (1977; read in the 1975 Haskins report), [LIT-904](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-904.md), read in [NOTE-826](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-826.md). Argued from Bernstein's degrees-of-freedom problem and Greene's equivalence classes, and supported at the spinal level by reflex-probe studies showing the segmental apparatus retuned in the tens of milliseconds before voluntary movement, and by Fel'dman's joint that goes to a preset equilibrium whatever its initial conditions. Its extension to all levels, and to tuning set directly by vision, is the author's speculation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-322](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-322.md) | The sense of agency over an action's outcome draws on prospective signals from action selection and outcome prediction, not only on retrospective comparison of outcome with prediction | Haggard (2017), [LIT-1009](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1009.md), read in full in [NOTE-827](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-827.md). A review, reporting a binding experiment in which action binding tracked the probability of a tone on trials with no tone, a patient study in which that prospective part was absent in schizophrenia, and priming studies in which ease of action selection raised the sense of control over an outcome it did not predict. It does not say the experience is accurate: the prospective part is by its nature blind to whether control was actually exercised. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-336](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-336.md) | An ideal observer is optimal relative to the information it is given, so a constrained ideal is the optimal decoder of a degraded input, not a restricted decoder of the full one; comparing real observers with ideals taken at successive stages of the visual system places losses by stage, and in early-vision tasks human performance is reported to parallel the retinal-stage ideal across conditions while falling well below it | Geisler (2011), [LIT-1055](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1055.md), read in [NOTE-870](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-870.md). A review that defines the ideal observer as optimal "given the available information and any specified constraints", and writes it as an expected-utility argmax over the posterior given the stimulus S or a constrained representation Z = g(S;θ). Constraints are added one at a time (optics, receptor sampling and noise, ganglion-cell summation), and human performance that parallels the retinal-stage ideal while falling below it is read as loss in central factors. The empirical parts are the review's account of studies the record has not read. The review gives no formula for efficiency and no notion of an optimum over a restricted class of computations. | Proposed |
